headline: Campsite and Backcountry Permits for Eastern Manitoba
reservation: While vehicle entry requires a standard Manitoba Provincial Parks pass, campsites in developed areas like Tulabi Falls must be reserved through the provincial parks reservation service. Backcountry water routes do not typically require a site-specific reservation but do require a valid park vehicle permit displayed at the trailhead or launch point. Check the official Manitoba Parks website for seasonal opening dates and fire restriction updates.

days.title: Shield Lakes and Cascades
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Lac du Bonnet

stops.name: Tulabi Falls
stops.detail: View the scenic waterfalls and utilize the accessible docks for a morning paddle on Tulabi Lake.

stops.name: Bird Lake
stops.detail: Launch here to explore the transition from the boreal forest to the rugged granite of the Canadian Shield.

days.driving: Allow 1–1.5 hours on gravel roads; conditions vary
days.note: Roads 314 and 315 are gravel and can be rough after heavy rain; check local conditions.

days.title: Boreal Backcountry Paddling
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the Bird River boat launch

stops.name: Bird River Canoe Route
stops.detail: Paddle through winding river sections and small portages that highlight the park's namesake 'Entrance to the Wilderness'.

stops.name: Elbow Lake
stops.detail: Reach this quiet backcountry destination known for its clear water and rocky islands.

days.note: Portage trails may be muddy; allow extra time for gear transfers between lakes.

days.title: Mining Heritage and High Ridges

stops.name: Walking Drum Trail
stops.detail: Hike through diverse forest stands to reach viewpoints overlooking the surrounding lake systems.

stops.name: Manigotagan River
stops.detail: Visit the upper reaches of this historic river corridor, a popular route for experienced wilderness paddlers.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes between trailheads; conditions vary
days.note: Watch for wildlife, including moose and woodland caribou, which are frequently spotted along the roadside.

intel.title: Trailhead Logistics
intel.text: Designated parking is available at Tulabi Falls and Black Lake, though these can fill during peak summer weekends. Always ensure your Manitoba Parks vehicle permit is clearly visible to avoid enforcement issues.

intel.title: Intermittent Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is unreliable once you travel north of Lac du Bonnet and is non-existent in most backcountry areas. Download offline maps before entering the park as digital navigation will fail.

intel.title: Last Service Points
intel.text: Lac du Bonnet is the primary hub for fuel, ice, and full groceries. Limited fuel may be found at seasonal resorts within the park, but availability is never guaranteed.

intel.title: Autumn Accessibility
intel.text: September offers fewer insects and vibrant fall colors, but be aware that some campground services may begin to scale back after the Labor Day weekend.

intel.title: Road Quality
intel.text: The park is accessed via PR 314 and PR 315, which are largely unpaved. These roads are subject to washboard conditions and dust; slow down for oncoming industrial traffic.

plan.arrival: Pickup supplies in Lac du Bonnet, ensure your Manitoba Parks vehicle pass is active, and proceed via Highway 315 to the Tulabi Falls area for initial check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars can manage the gravel roads, but an SUV provides better clearance for potholes. RVs should check for size restrictions at specific campsites.
plan.goldenHour: The sunset over Tulabi Lake from the cliff-top viewing platforms, particularly in late summer.
